title: Warmstart install — circuit-breaker observations and day-zero notes
content:
Purpose / context:
This is a working digest from the day-zero warmstart installs over the last week. Mostly notes from standups, quick triage threads, and action items for the install + networking team. Intended audience: field eng, SRE on-call, install Sherpas, and solutions eng.

Quick summary (TL;DR):
- Two recurring failure modes seen across 4 customer installs: 1) intermittent gRPC TLS handshake failures tied to SNI/cert chain ordering (particularly with older F5 appliances); 2) asymmetric MTU/path-MTU issues causing large initial KV cache fetches to time out and trigger circuit-breakers in the runtime.
- Workarounds deployed in-field: staged reduction of grpc max-message-size, aggressive probe/mtu settings, and temporary fallback to HTTP/1.1 proxying for the bootstrap path.
- Immediate actions: patch installer to detect path MTU and set net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing on bootstrap host (PR 421), add a cert-chain validation check to the preflight, and update runbook to include explicit L4 tests.

Standup notes (2027-03-22 -> 2027-03-25):
- 2027-03-22 09:15 — Quick sync (Priya/Ethan/Sofia)
  - Observed: customer "Orchid Health" install failed during node registration; stack: installer -> control-plane API over TLS. Logs show: "TLS handshake error: unknown certificate" intermittently.
  - Hypothesis: upstream load-balancer (vendor: F5) rewrites SNI or returns chained cert order that Go TLS library treats as invalid.
  - Short-term: added an explicit cert-chain ordering check in installer (local patch) and re-ran — passed.

- 2027-03-23 10:00 — Field standup (All field Sherpas)
  - Observed: at "NimblePay" cluster the runtime circuit-breaker trips during large config syncs (~1.2MB payloads) — errors look like gRPC DeadlineExceeded on first fetch.
  - Root cause: MTU fragmentation AND a combination of conservative grpc max-recv-size and proxy buffering (customer uses a haproxy that fragments payloads and delays reassembly).
  - Temporary mitigation: reduced initial payload to 300KB, enabled tcp_mtu_probing=1 on bootstrap nodes, and set GRPC_MAX_MESSAGE_LENGTH to 4MB for runtime after verifying memory footprint.

- 2027-03-24 16:30 — Escalation call (SRE + Eng + Customer NetEng)
  - Decision: for installs behind middleboxes we will run active L4 path-check (iperf3 + pmtu) as part of preflight. If MTU < 1400, switch bootstrap to chunked sync path (already implemented in branch warmstart-chunking).
  - Owner: Ethan to land warmstart-chunking branch. ETA 2027-03-28.

- 2027-03-25 11:00 — Postmortem sketch for "Greyline" failed install
  - Symptom: one node repeatedly failed post-install healthcheck; logs show "kv cache miss -> repeated retries -> circuit-breaker open".
  - Observation: customer network had middlebox performing deep packet inspection that dropped connections > 512KB until connection had been observed for ~20s. This caused retries and the runtime's circuit-breaker (threshold 5) to open.
  - Outcome: temporarily lowered circuit-breaker sensitivity for initial 60s window and added jitter to retry backoff.

Detailed customer blocker list (actionable):
- Orchid Health — cert-chain reordering with F5
  - Issue: TLS handshake fails intermittently during control-plane registration.
  - Evidence: installer logs + tcpdump show server returning 2 certs in non-standard order; Go TLS verifies leaf against CA and fails.
  - Action items:
    - Priya: add preflight cert-order check + fail with clearer message (PR opened). Due: 2027-03-26.
    - Sofia: prepare KB note for customer NetEng with pkcs7 extraction commands and recommended F5 config. Due: 2027-03-27.

- NimblePay — MTU + proxy buffering causing initial sync to fail
  - Issue: large bootstrap payloads hit proxy fragmentation; gRPC DeadlineExceeded triggers circuit-breaker.
  - Action items:
    - Ethan: ship warmstart-chunking (split payloads) and a preflight pmtu check. Linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/installer/pull/421. ETA: 2027-03-28.
    - Maya: field change — enable tcp_mtu_probing on customer bootstrap host as temporary measure. Command: sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1. Due: 2027-03-24 (done).

- Greyline — DPI middlebox causes long-tail connection drops
  - Issue: state syncs get observed/dropped, causing repeated backoffs and CB open.
  - Action items:
    - Team decision: implement initial-exempt window (60s) where circuit-breaker thresholds are relaxed for new nodes. Daniel to prototype. Due: 2027-03-29.
    - Solutions Eng to test packet pacing and small-chunk replays. Due: 2027-03-30.

Runbook / preflight updates (proposed):
- Add step: "Run simple MTU and pmtu test between bootstrap host and control-plane endpoint" with iperf3 and tracepath. Expected outputs + thresholds documented.
- Add step: "Validate cert-chain ordering and SNI behavior against vendor LB (F5/AKAMAI/NGINX)" with extraction commands and an example of bad vs good chain order.
- Add step: "Check for DPI/middlebox: run 3 transfers > 1MB and observe reassembly time; if reassembly > 5s, enable chunked warmstart."
- Add step: "Set temporary runtime circuit-breaker grace window: 60s after node registration" (config flag: runtime.initial_cb_grace_seconds).
- Add remediation CLI helpers: redwood-install preflight --mtu-check --cert-check --temp-cb=60

Operational knobs we changed (notes for SRE):
- runtime default: max-concurrent-syncs: 2 -> temporary bumped to 3 for warmstart windows.
- runtime circuit-breaker: failure-threshold: 5 -> temporarily 8 for first 60s during bootstrap.
- installer: grpc max-recv set to 4MB in warmstart path; chunking enabled when pmtu < 1400.

Open questions / unresolved:
- For customers with opaque middleboxes (managed by corp-net teams) we need a documented escalation path to request packet capture or to request a temporary bypass. Legal/compliance sometimes blocks us from capturing pcap on customer infra — need guidance from security.
- Should we make the initial-exempt window configurable in Hosted vs Private? (Proposal: default off for hosted, default on for private installs where middleboxes are common).

Meeting decisions (formalized):
- Add preflight MTU/cert checks to installer v0.9.3 (decision: ship with 0.9.3). Owner: Ethan.
- Add an entry to the private-deploy runbook named "Day-zero network oddities" with troubleshooting checklist and sample tcpdump filters. Owner: Sofia. ETA: 2027-04-02.

Action item tracker (short):
- Priya: PR for cert-order check + better error messages. Due 2027-03-26. (IN PROGRESS)
- Ethan: land warmstart-chunking + mtu probe; ensure CI tests cover chunked path. Due 2027-03-28. (IN PROGRESS; PR 421 open)
- Daniel: prototype initial CB grace window and unit tests. Due 2027-03-29.
- Sofia: KB + runbook updates; sample F5 commands and tcpdump filters. Due 2027-04-02.
- Maya: coordinate change window with NimblePay NetEng for permanent config. Due 2027-04-05.

Notes-to-self / field hints (quick copyable snippets):
- Extract full chain from endpoint: openssl s_client -showcerts -connect <host>:443 | sed -n '/BEGIN CERTIFICATE/,/END CERTIFICATE/p' > chain.pem
- Dump cert subjects quickly: for cert in $(csplit -f cert- chain.pem '/-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----/' '{*}' 2>/dev/null); do openssl x509 -in $cert -noout -subject; done
- PMTU probe: tracepath <host> (linux) or sudo iperf3 -c <host> -M 1200 -i 1 --logfile pmtu.log
- Temporary runtime flag for warmstart: --initial-cb-grace=60

Appendix: raw error snippets (sanitized)
- "rpc error: code = DeadlineExceeded desc = context deadline exceeded" (on first kv sync)
- "x509: certificate signed by unknown authority" followed by "certificate chain appears out-of-order" (installer log)
- tcpdump: "IP frag (proto 6) id 0x1c2a" repeated with no reassembly for ~10s

If you are on-call and see a new install failing with the above symptoms: escalate to #field-install immediately and @Priya. If topology looks like customer has an active middlebox, request NetEng join before changing production LB configs.

End of notes — will convert to a concise KB once PRs land and mitigations are validated in CI.
